title: Move a fridge shelf up a slot, tipping it to hook in
instruction: Move the glass shelf up one slot, to the blue-taped slots, level side to side, and let go.
context: Why: most people have moved a fridge shelf up or down a slot to fit a tall bottle or a pan. The knack: the shelf hangs by two hooks at the back, out of sight, and is held only by its front, 33 cm away. Carried in level, it never hangs: at any height either the hook tip meets the bar under its slot or the lower tab meets the bar above the slot below. The front has to be tipped up 8 degrees or more so the hooks swing in and drop, then lowered so the tabs swing into their slots. One hook a slot off leaves the shelf crooked. The makers say the same: Whirlpool, tilt the front up to lift the shelf out, guide the rear hooks into the supports, then lower the front; LG, make sure the shelf is level side to side or it may fall. Unlike lowering a bin straight down onto supports or carrying a drawer in above its rollers, here the level approach is the one that fails. Done by: whoever uses the fridge.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Fridge section, open at the front, centred on y 0 and clamped to the table: back wall cut from a ProWood 3/4 in sanded plywood project panel (18 mm), side walls and top from 1/2 in sanded plywood (12 mm), painted white; inside 42 cm wide (y -21 to 21), 34.5 cm deep, 47 cm tall; the walls' front edges at x 20.0, the back wall's inner face at x 54.5. A 1/2 in white polyethylene foam mat (Uline S-19391, cut 40 x 32 cm) lies on the floor inside. Two GE WR71X2588 cantilever shelf tracks (painted steel channel, 25 mm wide, 12 mm deep) are screwed upright to the back wall, centre lines 34 cm apart at y 17 and -17, front faces at x 53.3, from 2.5 to 46 cm up. Each has one column of 11 slot windows, 8 mm wide and 20 mm tall on a 38 mm pitch, at the same heights on both tracks, the lowest window's lower edge 3.3 cm up. Shelf: a GE WR32X10177 half-width cantilever glass shelf (sold as clearance stock; an in-production alternative is the Whirlpool WP2223288 cantilever shelf with glass, whose hooks are to be checked against the README's hook profile before use), 1.63 kg: 4 mm tempered glass 378 mm wide, a white ABS front trim 30 mm tall and 20 mm deep, and two painted steel brackets (3 mm plate) 34 cm apart whose rear edges are 333 mm behind the trim's front. Each bracket's rear edge has an upper hook (a neck 5 mm tall through a window, then a tip 3 mm thick turned down 8 mm below the neck, 1.5 mm behind the track's face) and, 22 to 27 mm below the neck, a straight tab 3 mm long that sits in the window below; the edge is cut back 5 mm for 20 mm under the hook, and below that it bears on the track's face. Start: the shelf hangs by both hooks in the 5th windows from the bottom (lower edges 18.5 cm up), its trim flush with the box front at x 20 and about 17.7 cm up, leaning about 1.6 deg front-down. Target: the 6th windows (lower edges 22.3 cm up), marked by a 24 x 50 mm strip of ScotchBlue 2090 painter's tape on the back wall beside each track, centred on the window. Friction (set, not measured): shelf 0.4, track and box 0.3. Both arms start in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run with a steel rule, a phone level, a 10 N spring scale, a torch photo through the glass at each hook, and the trial video. Engaged hook: its neck through a slot window, its underside on or within 3 mm above the window's lower edge, and its tip down behind the track's face reaching at least 4 mm below that edge (real trial: the torch photo, and a 10 N pull toward the robot at the trim's middle moves the shelf less than 3 mm). Target row: the taped windows, one slot (38 mm) above the start row. Level: the trim's two ends at heights within 3 mm of each other (steel rule from the box floor). Front lowered: the glass's front-to-back slope within 2 deg of its slope hung in the start row (phone level; the start is noted before the trial). Released and still: no gripper within 30 mm of the shelf, and no point of it moving more than 1 mm over the last 1 s (video). Held: a gripper within 10 mm of the shelf. Score 0 if, at any time, even if put back, the shelf falls (any point of it drops more than 45 mm in one 50 ms step, 0.9 m/s) or the fridge section moves more than 5 mm off its marks. Otherwise, at the end, the first that fits: 1.0 both hooks engaged in the target row, level, front lowered, released and still; 0.75 the same but still held or not yet still for 1 s; 0.5 both hooks engaged in one row other than the start row (the target row but not level or the front not lowered, or another row); 0.25 the hooks engaged in two different rows (hanging crooked), or neither hook in the start row with the shelf held up by a gripper; 0 anything else, including the untouched start, the shelf put back in the start row, or left on the floor. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.0 has held; only the end counts. Tipping, lifting out or re-hooking the shelf costs nothing.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted two-arm demo reaches full score in about 42 s (844 steps)
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Tip the shelf's front up, lift its hooks out of the windows, hang it back in the start windows (5th from the bottom) and lower the front; check both trim ends are at the same height within 1 mm on the rule, note the slope on the phone level, and check that a 10 N pull toward the robot at the trim's middle moves it less than 3 mm. Check the section and the tape are on their marks and put both arms in their ready pose. Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Rigid bodies; nothing is latched or moved by code: the hooks hold by contact under gravity. Shelf: one free body at catalogue size; hook, tab and window sizes are caliper estimates. 1.63 kg, about 1.5 kg real, raised because mass spreads by volume (centre of mass 148 mm behind the front, about 161 real), so the hands bear the real moment. Track face 2 mm (real about 1.2). Clamped section: a 40 kg free body. Friction static = dynamic. The 10 N pull is scored by the tip's 4 mm catch.
